description:
## Goal

After fz-kdt.4 deletes eager RuntimeDemand cone replay, make exact recursive-group publication membership reproducible across process hash seeds without changing semantic pull behavior.

## Construction order

fz-tfn.25 owns the work that is valid on the current graph: deterministic searches, candidate scans, reached candidates, dependency visits, and their causal telemetry. fz-kdt.5 then installs the cold/incremental product-work signal, fz-tfn.1 retains product state, and fz-kdt.4 removes the schedule-dependent eager cone interaction.

This ticket owns only the remaining exact member-identity requirement against that final reactive graph. It must not restore or preserve the old cone merely to stabilize its traversal order.

## Current evidence

Post-fz-kdt.47 runs have equal RuntimeDemand formula values, requested products, settled product sets, search-shape totals, and backend artifacts, but the eager cone/product interaction closes different exact pending SCC member sets involving union-typed versus narrower CallableConstruction activations. This is not a Ty alias defect and cannot be repaired by choosing a canonical resolver or sorting current pending members.

## TDD and acceptance

- Preserve the raw subprocess oracle that compares exact canonical recursive publication members.
- First prove it fails before the fz-kdt.4 cutover and becomes meaningful on the reactive per-executable graph.
- Exact successful recursive publication membership and canonical per-product group identity are reproducible across process hash seeds.
- Search counts and traversal work remain those established by fz-tfn.25; do not duplicate its traversal implementation or telemetry.
- Product values, settlements, backend programs, artifacts, and runtime output remain identical.
- Remove exclusions for recursive-member identity from the fz-kdt.5 causal report.
- Delete transition-only oracle data, switches, and compatibility paths before review.
- Update performance/fact-engine documentation and run targeted recursive-product, causal cross-process, target fixture, full library, matrix, formatting, and warning-free checks.

## Non-goals

Do not reintroduce cone collection, snapshot replay, private fixpoint passes, or ordering based on raw intern/hash identity.

comments.text: TDD implementation ready for cold review (uncommitted). Red: focused five-node pending graph failed on legacy early-exit reach work with left=1/right=5. Design deletes the separate reachability gate and repeated per-candidate SCC walks; one Tarjan traversal includes the prospective current->dependency edge, so it simultaneously detects the cycle and returns its members. Across 32 fresh RandomState memos the report is exact: candidate_scans=5, reached_candidates=2, dependency_reach_visits=5; a naive exhaustive-per-candidate rewrite would cost 41 SCC visits plus a separate gate. Checks: pull tests 31/31; full lib 1587 passed/5 ignored; target fixture interp/run/build 9/9; fz2_cli causal cross-process pass; clippy all-targets -D warnings pass; git diff --check pass. fz-kdt.5 must retain its JSONL/causal wiring and rerun its three-fixture cross-process acceptance after applying this structural diff.

Post-fz-kdt.47 evidence: RuntimeDemand formula values, requested products, settled product sets, search-shape totals, and backend artifacts are stable across processes, but the current eager cone/product interaction closes different exact pending SCC member sets (union-typed versus narrower CallableConstruction activations). This is not a Ty alias defect and cannot be repaired by choosing a canonical resolver or folding activation identity. Reactive per-executable RuntimeDemand in fz-kdt.4 must remove the schedule-dependent pending graph before this ticket can require exact stable group membership. The raw causal ledger and focused red subprocess oracle are preserved.

Authorized DAG split: fz-tfn.25 now owns current-graph recursive-search work determinism. This ticket retains exact recursive publication membership only, after fz-kdt.4 removes eager RuntimeDemand cone scheduling.

title: Make recursive-group publication membership reproducible after RuntimeDemand cutover
